title: DNA methylation remodeling and the functional implication during male gametogenesis in rice

predicted_errors.error_location: Results, section "CMT3a and CMT3b function during male gametogenesis" (Fig. 2b description vs. BS-seq methods sentence)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text states "The cmt3a mutants produced mainly defective pollens and were infertile (Fig. 2b)", yet the very next paragraph reports that BS-seq was performed on cells "isolated from two independent CRISPR/Cas9-free lines of cmt3a and/or cmt3b at T3-4 generation". Completely infertile homozygous mutants cannot be self-propagated to T3–T4 generations; the fertility statement contradicts the stated material source (and presumably should read partially sterile/reduced fertility).

predicted_errors.error_location: Results: "cmt3a pollen development was arrested likely at the bicellular microspore stage" vs. BS-seq of cmt3a sperm (Fig. 2c)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Sperm cells are only produced after the second pollen mitosis (tricellular stage). If cmt3a pollen development arrests at the bicellular stage, sperm cells should not be obtainable, yet the authors report BS-seq methylomes of cmt3a sperm ("cmt3a sperm mCHG (as well as mCHH) levels became higher than the mutant meiocyte (Fig. 2c)"). The phenotypic description and the sperm sampling are mutually inconsistent as written and require clarification (e.g., that only a minority of pollen develops normally).

predicted_errors.error_location: Results, paragraph on residual mCHG in cmt3a sperm (Additional file 1: Fig. S7b)
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The hypothesis that "the residual mCHG level in cmt3a sperm could be maintained by RdDM or CMT2" is claimed to be "supported by the observation that the drm2/cmt2 mutations also reduced the mCHG levels of those loci in leaves". Data obtained in a somatic tissue (leaves) cannot support a conclusion about which enzymes maintain methylation specifically in sperm of a cmt3a background; the supporting evidence does not test the stated hypothesis.
